Theorem
[closed collapsing manifolds are graph manifolds] Source: cao-zhu 1. Theorem 8.1\group Geometrization Suppose $(M^{\alpha },g^{\alpha }_{ij})$ is a sequence of compact orientable three-manifolds without boundary, and $w^{\alpha }\rightarrow 0$. Assume that for each point $x \in M^{\alpha }$ there exists a radius $\rho = \rho ^{\alpha }(x),$ not exceeding the diameter of the manifold, such that the ball $B(x,\rho )$ in the metric $g^{\alpha }_{ij}$ has volume at most $w^{\alpha }\rho ^3$ and sectional curvatures at least $-\rho ^{-2}$. Then $M^{\alpha }$ for sufficiently large $\alpha $ are diffeomorphic to graph manifolds.
